pr_title: root: Try to preserve relative positions of floating containers
pr_body:
Should fix https://github.com/swaywm/sway/issues/5308 and https://github.com/swaywm/sway/issues/6561. The translation behavior also applies to all floating containers (not just those on the scratchpad), since that's what i3 does.

I've been dogfooding this for the past week on a setup with monitors of different aspect ratios without issue.

`floating_fix_coordinates` is adapted from [the same in i3](https://github.com/i3/i3/blob/d26ddcbfe5f0ead61cc55c1f596692d9a89e71f9/src/floating.c#L799).

Seems like the floating point errors really start to compound after a few iterations

I'm only using one monitor though. Maybe it's related to smart_gaps then? I don't really mind the behavior when switching between different shaped monitors, there probably isn't a perfect solution for that.

I was able to reproduce it using smart_gaps. This was happening because with smart_gaps, a workspace with no windows  still has gaps enabled (so it ends up being smaller than a workspace with a single container).

I've changed the scratchpad-related transforms so that they use the output box instead of the workspace box. The transforms should be stable as long as we're restricted to a single output.

issue_context.title: Scratchpad window size is different on several outputs
issue_context.body:
When moving a window to scratchpad, it is resized. When it is shown on another output, it is resized again, even if the resolution is the same. 
Then it seems to keep the new size on all monitors.

If you resize it, the size is kept until you display it on another output.

The size seems to be different regarding the application.

sway version: 1.4

Config:
output DVI-I-1 pos 0,0 res 1920x1080
output HDMI-A-1 pos 1920,0 res 1920x1080
comments: I imagine it could be because of [this](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/5501d14a2e7147b533df12b21368639cf01a7c9c/sway/tree/root.c#L150) where it probably resizes too eagerly?
It does not happen with every windows. For example it happens with kitty but not with terminator.

I have the same problem

sway version 1.5.1

### Description:
In my case: [termite](https://github.com/thestinger/termite)
On startup I open a terminal in my scratchpad like:

```
set $term termite
exec $term --name $scratchterm
for_window [app_id="(?i)$scratchterm"] move to scratchpad, resize set 1800 1000 px, opacity set 0.9;
```

I have two monitors:

```
set $display1 DP-1
set $display2 HDMI-A-1
output $display1 pos 0 0 res 2560x1440
output $display2 pos 2560 0 res 1920x1080
output $display1 mode 2560x1440@143.998001Hz
output $display2 mode 1920x1080@60.000000Hz
```

When open scratchpad (`bindsym $mod+Return scratchpad show`) on my main display1 everything is correct set up (size: 1800x1000px). If I close and reopen scratchpad on the second screen the size has completely changed and is much smaller for the scratchpad terminal window. it doesn't matter on which display I create the scratchpad window, when I open it on the other screen the size of the scratchpad changes.

is my config wrong or is this a bug?
thank you.

@josefbachmann I've encountered this exact same issue independently (using alacritty), so I don't believe it's an issue with your configuration. It even happens if you use the default keybindings to place a floating terminal in the scratchpad and recall it on a different monitor.

I have the same use case as you for using the scratchpad and had to end up writing a `run-or-raise` style script that manually enforces the dimensions anytime the terminal is recalled from the scratchpad.

> [...] had to end up writing a `run-or-raise` style script that manually enforces the dimensions anytime the terminal is recalled from the scratchpad.

@gilbertw1 alrighty. Would you mind sharing the script (pastebin?) or some pointers how you did that? thank you very much.

@josefbachmann

Hey, I just put the script into a gist here: https://gist.github.com/gilbertw1/96a745cc9cf19c48052140ded4932253

Using the script, this is what I've got in my sway config:
```
    # Terminal Scratch
    for_window [title="scratchterm"] {
        floating enable
        resize set 3000 1800
        move position center
    }
    bindsym f12 exec sway-run-or-raise.sh "alacritty -t=scratchterm -d 0 0 -e ~/bin/tmuxp.sh" scratchterm 3000 1800 "center"
```

The script basically takes a command to run if the program isn't found, then a title used to find and match the program's window, followed by height and width, and then finally a position. I'm currently using center, but you could replace that with something like "100 200" for the x/y offset.

Just have the window size itself, this works fine for me 

```
for_window [title="scratchterm"] move scratchpad
exec kitty -o remember_window_size=no -o initial_window_width=50c -o initial_window_height=10c -T scratchterm
```

I've encountered  the same problem with kitty and some other applications. I don't think this is an expected behavior. Worked around by adding this to the config:
`bindsym --to-code $mod+minus [app_id="..."] scratchpad show, resize set 960 780, move position center`

UPD:
Well now I have a different problem. When hiding scratchpad, the next floating window get the focus and it gets resized and moved to center...

review_comments: If the old box is zeros, e.g. because the transform is unset or taken from fallback output geometry, we should handle it such that the client gets centered like a new window, as it did before.
